# Target.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/target-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/target-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product and store data from Target.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Target.com Product and Pricing Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-target-com)
- **Code:** [`target.py`](target.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Availability](results/availability.json) · [Product](results/product.json) · [Search](results/search.json) · [Store locations](results/store_locations.json) · [Stores](results/stores.json)

## What it scrapes

- Target product pages for product data, variants, pricing, and stock status
- Target search pages for product listing data
- Target RedSky API for product availability and fulfillment by store and zip code
- Target store sitemap for store location URLs
- Target RedSky API for store location details by store ID

## Functions

- `scrape_product(url)` → `Product`: scrape a Target product page and return parsed product data
- `scrape_availability(tcins, store_id, zip_code)` → `Dict`: scrape product availability and fulfillment data from product_summary_with_fulfillment_v1
- `scrape_store_locations_sitemap(url)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape store location URLs from the Target store sitemap
- `scrape_store_locations(store_ids)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape store location details from store_location_v1 for a list of store IDs
- `scrape_search(keyword, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape search results and paginate through all result pages

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import target


async def main():
    product = await target.scrape_product(
        "https://www.target.com/p/women-s-lace-godet-tank-top-wild-fable/-/A-95213693",
    )
    availability = await target.scrape_availability(tcins=["89231676"], store_id="1771", zip_code="52404")
    store_locations_sitemap = await target.scrape_store_locations_sitemap(
        url="https://www.target.com/sl/sitemap_0001.xml.gz",
    )
    store_locations = await target.scrape_store_locations(store_ids=["3", "4"])
    search = await target.scrape_search(keyword="laptop", max_pages=3)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`Price`**: `current_retail?`, `reg_retail?`, `formatted_current_price?`, `location_id?`
- **`ProductVariant`**: `tcin`, `price?`, `free_shipping`, `in_stock`
- **`Product`**: `tcin`, `title?`, `rating?`, `review_count?`, `variants`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`target.py`](target.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/target-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_availability_scraping`, `test_store_locations_sitemap`, `test_store_locations`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
